decisions.issues: Clean. Matches the beat: dusk hill under mango trees, a low two-tiered tiled gateway near the crown, the stone stair, a small party of torch-bearing Nair guards and horses with nobody readable as a rider, no banners or palanquin, no painted text. The open dusk sky across the upper left and centre gives plenty of room for both captions.

Acceptable with minor misses. Varma's knot sits high at the back of the crown rather than clearly above his LEFT ear. The sandal-paste line on his brow is not visible. His seat on the horse is a little ambiguous because the mundu hides his leg. Ramayyan wears a tiny ear stud that his sheet does not show. Everything else holds: Varma is bare-headed with no crest or spear, wears pearl drop earrings and one gold chain, and has a cream mundu with a gold border. Ramayyan has his receding hair, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus, and looks up at the king. No text. The dusk sky at the upper centre-left holds both balloons.

Acceptable with minor misses. A faint thin orange vertical stroke at the centre of Nagoji's brow could read as a sandal mark, and the script asks for no forehead mark. It is about 3 px wide and almost invisible at reading size. Varma's face is a little rounder and younger than in panels 2, 4 and 5. His hair is wavy, with the knot at the back of the head rather than clearly above the LEFT ear. His single gold chain is a plain rope where the neighbouring panels show beads, and his brow has no sandal line. The dismount is caught mid-motion: he is still in the saddle, leaning forward with his bare foot out of the stirrup reaching down, not swinging a leg over. Some Nair guards stand up on the stair, and the gateway sits closer than in panel 1. Everything else holds and fixes the r1 failures. Varma is bare-headed with pearl drop earrings, one gold chain and a cream gold-bordered mundu, with no crest, spear or turban. He passes the reins to the turbaned stable boy while looking away. The heir, about ten, sits mounted behind on his own horse with wide watchful eyes, a topknot and a thin gold chain. Nagoji is at the right edge of the torchlight: high topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold stud, silver chain, plain cream shoulder cloth. A long pale scar runs along his left forearm, with no dark sigil, and he is unarmed and uninjured. No text, no gore. The open dusk sky in the upper left is clear for Varma's balloon.

Acceptable. The sandal-paste line on Varma's brow is not visible, and he has a cream cloth over one shoulder (still bare-chested, not forbidden). Otherwise strong: Varma's profile matches the varma-v1 face study, with hair tied in a knot behind the left ear, a pearl drop earring, one gold chain, no crest and no spear. Ramayyan matches his sheet (receding hair, white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus) and faces the king closely. The Nair guards stand behind them. No text. The upper-left sky and foliage above Ramayyan hold both balloons without touching faces.

Acceptable with minor misses. Varma's knot sits at the back of his head, with loose curls at the nape, rather than clearly above the LEFT ear (panel 2 has the same). Below Nagoji's topknot, his hair hangs in loose curls to the shoulders. His pale scar runs from the upper arm across the elbow, not only along the inner forearm. Lettering room is only fair. Varma's balloon can sit over the dark foliage at upper left, between his head and the torch flames. Ramayyan's long balloon fits the sky and palms across the top centre-right, but it is pinched by Nagoji's head and may overlap the edge of the distant gateway. Otherwise strong, and the r1 failures are fixed. Varma has a lean face consistent with panels 2 and 4, black hair tied back, a pearl drop earring, a white sandal line on his brow, one beaded gold chain and a cream gold-bordered mundu, with no crest, spear or turban. He stands on the left, turned toward Ramayyan. Ramayyan stoops mid-bow in the middle, head turned toward Nagoji: receding curly hair, thin features, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus. Nagoji waits at the right edge of the torchlight: high topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold stud, silver chain, plain shoulder cloth, no brand blot, unarmed and uninjured. The Nair guards are settled with their torches at the foot of the lit stair, with horses and a stable boy behind. Hands are sound, and there is no text or gore.

Minor: Varma's hair is mostly loose curls, with only a loosely gathered mass above his LEFT ear standing in for the side knot. He wears a vertical white namam where the script asks for a horizontal sandal line. Over-the-shoulder framing, Nagoji's topknot, grey temples, flush gold stud and silver chain, the pearl drops and single gold chain, and the dusk torchlit stair setting all match. The two balloons fit in the sky and canopy at upper centre, between the two heads.

Minor: this is a medium close-up, chest up, not a tight face close-up. Otherwise it is clean: thick curled moustache, clean chin, grey temples, high topknot, tiny flush stud, no forehead mark, and a wry, almost-smile expression. The caption fits in the clear dusk sky at upper left.

Minor: a torch is mounted on a post at frame left, where the setting asks for no posts. Varma's knot sits at the back of his crown and is not clearly above the LEFT ear, which is turned away from camera. Varma and the heir carry namam marks rather than a sandal line. The beat reads well: Varma climbs ahead looking up at the bare rock, the heir is at his side, and Nagoji follows behind, unarmed, with the scar showing on his inner left forearm. The balloon fits over the night sky and grey rock face at upper centre.

Minor: Varma's hair is a topknot on the crown, not a side knot (this matches page 1 panels 1.2 and 1.4). Varma and the heir stand beside the jackfruit tree rather than directly under it, and they face camera rather than the sanctum; the boy's eyes do turn up-left toward it. The lingam inside is clearer than 'faintly'. Every other script element is present: the jasmine-hung sanctum, lamp niches in the peeling lime-wash, the roots heaving the flags, the cropped-hair assistant with a torch and a basket of ghee pots, and the sleeping dog. The long caption fits over the plain foreground stone at bottom left, or over the stone floor at bottom centre-right.

Minor: Varma's face is a little rounder and younger than the varma-v1 sheet. He wears a vertical namam rather than a sandal line. This is the best match of the page for the side knot: it sits above his LEFT ear with a pearl drop below. His hand rests soundly on the heir's shoulder as he turns toward off-panel right with a sly half-smile. The boy keeps his palms pressed, with eyes wide toward the doorway. The marks on the lingam are three ash stripes, not pseudo-text. The long balloon fits over the night sky and mandapa roofline at upper centre, or the plain lime-washed wall below it.

Minor only. The long white scar is drawn on the upper arm near the elbow rather than along the forearm next to the brand. The brand itself is a correct pale puckered patch on the inner LEFT forearm with no letters. The old priest's cloth has orange-red border stripes, while panel 3.2 shows his hands with a cream cloth and a gold border. Nagoji's topknot sits loosely on curly hair but reads as a crown knot. Varma has black hair, a pearl earring and is stooping at the sanctum. The heir is in a white mundu with a topknot. The lingam is ash-marked. There is clear night sky and leaves across the top middle for both captions.

Minor only. In the old priest's inset his cloth has a gold border, but panel 3.1 shows orange-red border stripes, a small costume mismatch. The out-of-focus lingam in inset 3 has textured ash stripes that only read as faint marks at high zoom; at print size they read as ash. Inset 1's wrist is walking along the steps rather than clearly down them. The four insets are correct: bangled wrist, cropped-hair bare-chested assistant with torch, priest's hands with wick and ghee lamp, sleeping dog. There is dark sky in the upper part of inset 1 for the caption.

Minor only. The chaver has a small red vertical mark through the three ash stripes, which the close-up in 3.4 does not show. Otherwise correct: young and clean-shaven with an ordinary face, low nape knot, white cloth over the LEFT shoulder, sacred thread, brass plate with flowers and clay lamp, no dagger. He steps out of the lit side-room door with his gaze off the left edge, and the sanctum is out of view. There is clear night sky at the upper left and middle for the caption.

Minor only. This extreme close-up fills the strip, so the whole head is larger than the frame; the face circle encloses the eyes and stripes only. The hair at the temples falls loose and curly rather than oiled back, and the red mark seen in 3.3 is absent. The eyes are still, unblinking and looking toward the left, lit warmly from below, with three thick ash stripes. Both captions must sit in the dark corners: top or far left (background and hair) and top or far right (hair and shadow), clear of the eyes and stripes.

Minor only. The gap between the two men is a little wider than arm's length, the chaver reads slightly older than in 3.3, and the niche-lamp flames barely bend. Otherwise clean: Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch22 row (high topknot with grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold stud, silver chain with medallion, shoulder cloth, scar on the inner left forearm, unarmed, barefoot) and stands under the jackfruit tree at right, watching. The chaver is at left, clean-shaven, with three ash stripes, a knot at the nape, a sacred thread and cloth over his left shoulder. He walks left toward the sanctum without looking at Nagoji, and the plate lamp burns straight up. There is no painted text, blade, blood or anachronism. Open sky and wall in the upper centre (about x 0.40 to 0.66, y 0.0 to 0.2) leave room for the balloon, and the caption can go top-left or on the lower floor.

Minor only: the chaver's mouth is nearly closed rather than visibly speaking; Varma and the boy wear a vertical namam rather than a horizontal line of sandal paste; the lamp on the plate is brass rather than clay; the boy stands mid-courtyard rather than right at the sanctum threshold. Faces, costume, three-figure count, setting (jasmine sanctum left, peeling lime-wash wall with niche lamps, jackfruit tree right) and the dark upper sky/wall for the balloon and two captions are all sound.

Acceptable with small deviations: the chaver shows light stubble along the jaw (script says clean-shaven), bushier hair than in 4.1, and no ash stripes on his arm; the dagger is held reverse-grip at his hip pointing down rather than laid back along the forearm; Nagoji wears a plain silver bangle on his right wrist and carries the same heavy grey at the temples as on page 3. The beat is clear: plate, flowers and clay lamp falling, dagger in the chaver's left hand, Varma (black hair, side knot, pearl earrings, one gold chain, no crest or spear) planted with arms wide, the heir behind him, Nagoji launching by the tree. No painted text.

Minor only. The temple assistant has three ash stripes on his brow, a sacred thread and a white cloth over one shoulder, but his figure tag says no ash and no shoulder cloth. He is still clearly identified by the torch, his close-cropped hair and his open shouting mouth. Varma's hair is loose and curly with faint grey highlights and a knot near the crown on his left side, not a sleek side knot. This matches how he is drawn in the 4.2 frame. Everything else fits the beat: the shot is from behind the chaver (white cloth over his left shoulder, knot at the nape, sacred thread), the assistant hurls himself in from the mandapa side with the torch raised and hides the blade completely, Varma stands braced with his arms wide (pearl drops, one gold chain, moustache), and the jasmine sanctum is at left with the jackfruit tree at right. There is no text, blood or anachronism. The dark sky at top centre is clear for the 'Shiva!' balloon.

Minor: the assistant reads more as falling forward onto hands and knees than fully crumpling, and the torch is lying still rather than visibly rolling. Otherwise clean. Low angle, he is in silhouette, close-cropped hair, bare-chested, no shoulder cloth, and no wound. The fallen torch spills light across the flags. The courtyard matches 4.5: sanctum with jasmine at left, jackfruit tree at right, niche lamps, side door. No text and no lettering needed.

Minor continuity: the dagger is a straight, single-edged knife held point-forward in the chaver's right hand. In 4.2 it is a slender reversed blade in his left hand, but it reads as a mid-struggle regrip. The hands at the hilt are slightly busy but readable: Nagoji's left hand clamps over the chaver's fist and wrist. Nagoji matches the sheet and the bible row. He has a high topknot with grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a small gold stud, a silver chain with a pendant, and the scar and brand on his inner left forearm with no letters. The chaver matches his tag: clean-shaven, three ash stripes, a low knot at the nape, a sacred thread and cloth over his left shoulder. Screen direction is correct (Nagoji right, chaver left), and the dog bolts mid-bark in the background. Clear dark sky at top centre (about x 0.30 to 0.55, y 0 to 0.12) takes the short caption, away from the inset in the upper left.

Acceptable; this fixes the r1/r2 failures. The old priest is now visibly elderly, with grey hair and ash stripes. He stands at the mandapa pillar on the sanctum side at screen LEFT, gripping the heir's arm and hauling him behind it. Varma, half turning toward the off-panel struggle at right, shoves the boy back toward the sanctum by the shoulder. He matches his ch22 row: bare-headed, pearl drop earring, one thin gold chain, bare chest, cream gold-bordered mundu, no crest and no spear. The heir is about ten, wide-eyed and staring, with a small topknot, a thin gold chain and a white mundu. The setting matches 5.2 and 5.3: jasmine-hung sanctum with a faint lingam at left, peeling lime-washed wall with niche lamps, jackfruit tree and roots at right, night. There is no text and no blood. Minor: because of the three-quarter view, Varma's knot reads as back or far side of the crown rather than clearly above the left ear. The priest's and boy's interlocked hands at the pillar are a little muddled at small size. For the three short captions, the sky at upper centre (x 0.42 to 0.58, top 18%) and the plain wall at upper right are clear.

Acceptable. Nagoji is on the right and matches his sheet and bible row: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold stud, high topknot with grey at the temples, silver chain, cream mundu and shoulder cloth. His LEFT hand is locked on the chaver's dagger wrist with the dagger trembling between them. The chaver on the left is clean-shaven, with ash stripes, sweat and bared teeth. There is no painted text and no blood. Minor: the chaver's costume and hair do not follow the script (ochre torn sleeveless top, red sash and loose long curls, instead of white cloth over the left shoulder, a sacred thread and a knot at the nape). This does match his brown top and red sash in 4.3 and 4.5. The brand on Nagoji's inner left forearm is a small dark round stamp-like mark next to the white scar, not a pale puckered patch, but it has no readable letters. Caption space: the sky and wall top along the upper band, plus the leaves at upper right or the floor and roots at lower right.

Acceptable. Exactly one dagger this time. The chaver (left, clean-shaven, ochre torn tunic, red sash, white lower cloth) drives his bent dagger-arm elbow into Nagoji's side under the chest, while Nagoji (right) winces and folds around it, his LEFT hand clamped on the chaver's dagger fist and the blade pointing down and away. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch22 row: thick curled moustache, clean chin, tiny gold stud, high topknot with grey temples, silver chain with medallion, cream mundu and shoulder cloth. The brand on his inner left forearm is a pale puckered patch with no letters. Same courtyard and lighting as 5.2. Minor: Nagoji's grip sits on the fist and hilt rather than strictly on the wrist. The chaver's hair is shorter than in 5.2 and his ash stripes are hidden by hair and the turned brow. The sky and wall-top band at upper centre (x 0.52 to 0.70, top 16%) holds the medium caption clear of both faces.

Acceptable tight insert. Nagoji's LEFT arm comes from screen left (silver chain and cream shoulder cloth at the edge), palm toward the viewer with the thumb up, which is correct for a left hand. The brand is a pale puckered patch with the long white scar on the inner forearm and no letters. His hand has slid down onto the chaver's dagger fist: the thumb still hooks over the knuckles and the fingers still curl around beneath, while the blade's point lies across the heel of his open palm. That reads as slip, still holding, no cut. No blood, no text, and the night courtyard background (sanctum, niche lamps, tree roots) matches. Minor: the brand sits mid-forearm rather than near the wrist. No lettering is needed.

v01 (the only candidate): wrong cast. The attacker holding the dagger on the left has Nagoji's captivity look: thick moustache, gold ear stud, long loose curls, torn ochre tunic and bandaged wrists. He is not a clean-shaven chaver. The figure on the right, with a pearl drop earring and a gold bead necklace, is Varma, and he is the one gripping the attacker's wrist. Ananthan Pillai (topknot with grey temples, silver chain, cream mundu and shoulder cloth) is missing entirely, so Nagoji's LEFT hand dragging on the chaver's wrist is not shown. The panel reads as Nagoji attacking the king. It also breaks screen direction: Varma should come in from the left (6.1, 6.3) with Nagoji on the right.
decisions.correction: Draw exactly THREE men, with no doubles. LEFT: Marthanda Varma, with the face, moustache and heavier build from his sheet, black hair in a side knot above his LEFT ear, pearl drop earrings, ONE thin gold chain, bare chest, cream mundu with a thin gold border, no turban, no crest, no spear. He steps IN toward the blade, weight driving forward, front foot advancing, hands rising, calm and set; he does not lean back. CENTRE: the chaver, a young, lean, wiry stranger, CLEAN-SHAVEN with NO moustache, NO ear ornament and NO wrist bandages, three thick white horizontal ash stripes across his forehead, short dark curly hair, in the same ochre sleeveless top, dark red sash and white lower cloth as the previous panels. He thrusts his single dagger upward, its point aimed at Varma's throat a hand-span short of it, never touching it. RIGHT: Nagoji as Ananthan Pillai: high Kerala topknot with first grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, CLEAN-SHAVEN chin, tiny flush gold ear stud, silver chain, cream mundu with a gold-bordered shoulder cloth, bare arms, no bandages, never the torn ochre captivity tunic. His LEFT hand is locked on the chaver's dagger wrist, dragging it back toward the right. The dagger is the only blade, and there is no blood. Keep the night courtyard with the sanctum and jasmine at screen left, the niche lamps on the peeling lime-washed wall, the jackfruit tree at screen right and the warm lamplight.

decisions.issues: v01 is the wrong beat and has no chaver at all. Only two men are drawn. Varma holds the dagger himself and drives his hand into NAGOJI's throat, while Nagoji grips Varma's wrist, so it reads as the king attacking Nagoji. Varma's hair is a bun on the crown, not a side knot above his LEFT ear. The courtyard, lamps, tree and Nagoji's look (moustache, grey temples, silver chain, stud) are otherwise good.
decisions.correction: Draw THREE men, not two. The chaver, the assassin, stands in the CENTRE and holds the only dagger. He is young, lean and wiry, CLEAN-SHAVEN with no moustache, with three thick horizontal white ash stripes across his forehead and oiled black hair tied in a tight knot low at the nape. He wears white cloth at the waist and over his LEFT shoulder, plus a thin sacred thread. His dagger arm thrusts up toward Varma. Varma is at screen LEFT, inside the dagger's arc: face from the varma sheet, black hair in a side knot above his LEFT ear, pearl drop earrings, one gold chain, bare chest, cream mundu with a thin gold border, and no weapon. His left hand clamps the CHAVER's forearm. His right hand drives stiff-fingered into the CHAVER's throat in a kalari strike, with a calm, practised face. Varma never holds the dagger and never touches Nagoji. Nagoji is at the right edge: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, high topknot, grey temples, silver chain, cream shoulder cloth. His LEFT hand stays locked on the chaver's dagger wrist just below Varma's grip, and he is not being struck. Keep this version's courtyard, niche lamps, sanctum at left, jackfruit tree at right and the open dark sky in the upper centre for one long caption.

decisions.issues: Acceptable, with minor misses. The beat reads clearly: the clean-shaven chaver (horizontal ash stripes, knot at the nape, sacred thread, white cloth over the shoulder) snaps his forehead into Varma's brow, and Varma reels back a step, eyes shut. Varma is bare-headed with no crest or spear, with his face and moustache from the sheet, a pearl drop earring, one gold bead chain, bare chest and a cream mundu with a gold border. There is no text and no blood. Minor: Varma's brow mark is the sheet's vertical namam, its red centre smeared at the impact. It is not the horizontal sandal-paste line seen in 6.3, but the namam has been tolerated elsewhere in this chapter. The red smear stays inside the mark and reads as kumkum, not a wound. His knot sits on the top and back of his head, not above the LEFT ear (tolerated in this chapter). The chaver's dagger hand hangs free and low at the lower right, with no grip on it. Both captions fit in the dark sky and the plain lime-washed wall at the upper centre-right, clear of both heads.

Acceptable, with minor misses. It fixes the r1 failures: the left-to-right staging holds, with Varma recoiling at the left edge, the chaver in the middle and Nagoji at right. The chaver is clean-shaven and bare-chested, with ash stripes, a nape knot, a sacred thread and white cloth. Varma has black hair, no grey, his moustache with upturned points, a pearl drop, one gold chain, a bare chest and no crest or spear. Nagoji matches his sheet and ch22 row: thick curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold stud, high topknot, grey temples and silver chain. His RIGHT hand lies over his LEFT, and the long scar is on the LEFT forearm only. The dagger point stops about a hand-span from Varma's jaw and chin. There is no text and no blood. Minor: Nagoji's two hands catch the chaver's upper arm near the shoulder rather than the wrist. The dagger hilt has a second fist behind the first, which reads as the chaver's two-handed grip. Varma's sandal-paste line is intact, not smeared. His knot sits at the back of his head rather than above the LEFT ear (tolerated in this chapter). The panel has no lettering.

Minor issues only. The chaver wears a red waist sash where the bible gives white cloth. The lamplight falls more from the side than from below. Nagoji's brand sits on the top of his left forearm rather than the inner side. Otherwise clean: Nagoji on the right has a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a gold stud, a high topknot, grey temples and a silver chain. The chaver on the left is clean-shaven with ash stripes and a knot at the nape, and the faces are inches apart with arms tangled high on the dagger. The two captions can sit top-left over the mandapa lintel and top-right over the sky.

Minor only. The chaver is young and clean-shaven, with three smeared ash stripes, hair tied at the nape and white cloth over his LEFT shoulder. The courtyard (sanctum left, niche lamps, jackfruit tree right) matches the page. His eyes show white all round small irises rather than blown pupils, so the look edges slightly toward fright, though the open grin reads as fierce joy. The face is rendered softer and more painterly than the inked neighbouring panels. The dark sky upper right gives clear room for the two short balloons, away from the face.

Acceptable. Nagoji is on the right and matches his sheet and the ch22 row: high topknot, grey at the temple, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, flush gold stud, silver chain, white mundu and shoulder cloth with a gold border. His forehead snaps into the clean-shaven chaver's cheekbone and the chaver's head recoils, with no injury drawn. The room and lighting match page 6. One minor deviation: the chaver wears a long-sleeved tan shirt with a brown sash and loose curly hair, and no ash stripes show. The script tag calls for a bare chest, white cloth, a knot at the nape and ash stripes. Neighbouring panels draw him inconsistently anyway. The short caption can sit top left on the shrine entablature or in the dark sky and wall at the top centre and right.

Acceptable. It follows the r1 correction. The screen direction holds: the chaver is on screen LEFT in a white waist cloth with a rust-brown sash end, and Nagoji is on screen RIGHT in a white mundu with a gold border hem. The chaver's heel splashes and skids through the glossy oil smear. Nagoji's bare foot pushes in behind the chaver's heel and ankle. The tipped clay lamp is still burning, and crushed jasmine and red flowers lie in the oil. The shrine and lingam are at left and the jackfruit tree at right, all at night. There is no text or blood, and the visible feet are anatomically sound. Minor: the hook reads as Nagoji's toes and forefoot pressing behind the heel rather than a full instep curl, but the trip still reads. No lettering is needed.

Acceptable. Nagoji is slammed prone on the flags with his near (RIGHT) shoulder on the stone and his right arm crumpled under him. His left hand is flat, palm down and clean. His face is contorted. He matches the sheet and the ch22 row: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold stud, grey temples, a topknot bun on the crown, the silver chain, and a white shoulder cloth and mundu with a gold border. The chaver tumbles on top of him, teeth bared. He is clean-shaven, with three white ash stripes, a sacred thread and a white cloth over his shoulder. The dagger is still in his hand, which feeds 7.4. The setting matches the page: sanctum and lingam at left, niche lamps, the side door, the jackfruit tree at right, night. Minor: the chaver's knot sits at the back of the head rather than low at the nape, and he keeps the rust-red sash seen in 6.4 and 7.2. The caption fits in the dark sky at top centre, above the wall.

Minor only. The background figures are drawn sharp, not out of focus as the script asks. Nagoji's right arm lies stretched forward on the flags instead of hanging limp, so it reads as weight-bearing; this is soft because he is a background figure and the pose sets up 8.2 (crawling, LEFT hand reaching for the hilt). The whole floor glistens heavily wet. The 2.3 stair is described as wet stone, so this is plausible, but it is glossier than the dry flags in 7.1, 7.3 and 7.5. The dagger is straight with an ornate brass hilt, where the script calls for a slightly curved blade. Otherwise clean. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch22 bible row: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny gold stud, high topknot, grey at the temples, silver chain, cream mundu with shoulder cloth. The chaver is clean-shaven, with ash stripes, a knot at the nape and cloth over his LEFT shoulder, consistent with 7.3 and 7.5. The courtyard (mandapa with jasmine and lingam at left, niche lamps, jackfruit roots at right) matches the neighbouring panels. The dagger rests against the pillar foot in niche-lamp light, with a spin trail on the flags. No painted text, blood or anachronism. Hands are sound. No lettering is needed.

Acceptable. It follows the r1 correction. Nagoji lies on his back on bare flags with his RIGHT arm flung out limp. His LEFT hand pushes at the chaver's chest with the palm hidden, so no cut and no blood show. He matches the sheet and bible row: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, flush gold stud, grey temples, hair gathered at the crown, silver chain. The chaver is on top of him. He is clean-shaven and young, with three white ash stripes, a knot at the nape and white cloth over his left shoulder. One hand claws at Nagoji's jaw and throat, and the other balls into a fist drawn back low by his ribs. There is no stray cloth or pole. The setting matches the page: shrine and lingam at left, niche lamps, the side door, the jackfruit tree at right, night. Minor: from the chaver's facing, the fist is technically his left hand rather than the scripted right. Nagoji's crossing arm is steeply foreshortened and roots close to the near shoulder, but it reads as his left arm. The chaver has lost the rust-red sash he wore in 7.3. The caption fits at the top in the dark sky and upper wall, between the shrine roof and the jackfruit leaves and above the chaver's head.

Acceptable, with two minor misses. Varma's black hair has grey streaks at the temple and behind the ear, against the MUST MATCH 'black hair, never grey'. The grey is lighter than in r1 v01 and about the same as in the already-accepted p12-p2. His knot sits at the back of the crown, not above the LEFT ear, which this chapter has tolerated before (p1-p2, p2-p3, p2-p4). No sandal paste shows on his brow. Everything r1 asked for is now fixed. The chaver's hands are empty with no dagger. He is young, lean and clean-shaven with white horizontal ash stripes, in a white waist and shoulder cloth with a sacred thread, and his body folds around Varma's side-kick to the ribs. The red namam is gone. Varma wears pearl drop earrings and one gold chain, bare-chested in a cream mundu with a gold border, with no crest and no spear. The courtyard matches the setting: jasmine sanctum at screen left, peeling lime-wash wall with niche lamps, jackfruit tree at screen right. There is no text, blood or anachronism. The long caption fits in the dark night-sky band at top centre between the shrine roof and the tree, clear of Varma's head.

Acceptable. The r1 failures are fixed. Nagoji is now in ch22 dress: bare-chested with a cream shoulder cloth with a gold border. He has grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a small flush gold stud and the silver chain. His LEFT arm reaches to the screen right and closes around the dagger's hilt at the pillar's foot. A pale puckered brand patch with a thin white scar sits on that forearm, not a crisp tattoo. The wall shadow now clearly reads as two silhouettes: Varma, knotted hair, kneeling over the pinned chaver with his fist in the chaver's hair, thrown large by the fallen torch on the flags. Minor points: Nagoji's hair is half-loose curls with only a small knot on the crown, not a tidy high topknot. His right arm is tucked under his chest with the fist on the stone, not clearly hanging. A red-and-gold striped cloth lies spread under the fallen torch. It is not in the script, but it reads as fabric, not blood. The generator painted two flat blank patches, one in the shadow and one on the wall to its right. Lettered captions will cover them. 'Once.' and 'Twice.' can sit on the large flat shadow. The warm-metal caption fits on the clear floor strip below the forearm and hand. No text in the art.

v01 (only candidate): the beat is wrong. The chaver is missing, and Nagoji lies on his back under Varma in the chaver's place, raising the dagger from below, so it reads as Varma pinning Nagoji. Nagoji should be up on one knee on the RIGHT, separate from the pair, with his right arm hanging limp. Varma also has grey-streaked hair, but black hair is required.
decisions.correction: Three separate men must be in the frame. 1) The chaver: young, lean, CLEAN-SHAVEN with no moustache, three thick horizontal ash stripes across his forehead, oiled hair in a low knot at the nape, white waist cloth. He lies pinned on his back on the flags, arching his bare chest upward toward the dagger's point, eyes fixed on the steel. 2) Varma, kneeling over the chaver at left centre with his RIGHT shoulder bearing down on the chaver's chest: fully BLACK hair with no grey, side knot above his LEFT ear, smeared sandal paste across the brow, one gold chain, pearl drop earrings, cream mundu with a thin gold border. 3) Nagoji, apart from them on the RIGHT side of the frame, up on ONE KNEE and not lying down or under anyone. He has a high topknot, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a silver chain, a cream mundu and a shoulder cloth. His right arm hangs limp at his side and the dagger is raised high in his LEFT fist above the chaver's chest. Nagoji must never be the man pinned under Varma. Keep the courtyard (sanctum with jasmine at screen left, lamp niches, jackfruit roots at right), the warm lamplight and open upper wall and sky for two captions.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. This is a tight insert of Nagoji's LEFT forearm and hand coming in from screen left, with the cream shoulder cloth at the edge. The palm side faces the camera: fingernails curl toward us with the thumb over the guard, five digits, sound anatomy. On the inner forearm the brand is now a pale puckered patch of raised scar ridges with a thin white scar beside it. It is not a tattoo or symbol and has no letters, which fixes the r1 failure. The blade angles up and away, out of the top-right corner, and no body, chest or cloth touches it. There is no blood and no red. The soft courtyard behind matches the page: jasmine sanctum and lingam at left, lamp niches, jackfruit roots at right. Minor points: the dagger hilt here is ornate engraved brass, while 8.2 has a dark wrapped grip with brass fittings. The arm enters from screen left while the script puts Nagoji on the right in 8.3, though it matches 8.2's left-to-right reach. The two captions can sit in the dark sky band at top centre-right and on the plain lit wall at right above the hand, or low on the stone floor at the bottom left-centre.

Acceptable with reservations. It is a floor-level upward view with jackfruit leaves black against a starry night sky and lamp glow, and it keeps screen direction (sanctum left, jackfruit right). However, it shows much of the empty courtyard, so it reads partly as an establishing shot rather than a dying man's upward gaze. The frame is not tilted and its edges are not soft; the layout should rotate it slightly and add an edge vignette or blur. The chaver is the off-panel POV speaker, so the small fading balloon sits in the open sky at upper centre with its tail toward the bottom edge.

v01 (the only candidate): Varma, kneeling at right, is drawn with the young clean-shaven face of the temple-priest sheet: no moustache, white ash stripes and a red dot on the brow. It is not the moustached varma-v1 face that 9.3 to 9.5 and pages 4 to 10 use. Nagoji has a faint mark on his forehead, and his brand reads as red bands that look like fresh cuts. The rest works: the high angle through the leaves; the chaver face down with no blood; Nagoji kneeling with the dagger in his left hand; the grey-bearded old priest's arm locked around the heir at the sanctum door; the dog against the far wall; caption room in the top foliage and wall.
decisions.correction: Varma, kneeling back from the chaver's body on the right of the courtyard, must have the face from the varma-v1 sheet: a thick black curled moustache, a mature man in his thirties with a heavier build, black hair gathered in a side knot above his LEFT ear, pearl drop earrings, one gold chain and a cream mundu with a thin gold border. He must NOT have the young clean-shaven face of the temple-priest sheet. There are no ash stripes and no red dot on his brow, only a line of white sandal paste, smeared and broken (no blood). The old grey-bearded priest holding the heir is the only figure who takes the priestly look. Nagoji has no mark of any kind on his forehead. The brand on his inner left forearm is a pale puckered patch with one thin white scar line, never red bands that read as fresh cuts. Keep everything else exactly as it worked: the high angle from inside the jackfruit canopy; the chaver face down on the flags, bare-chested with no blood; Nagoji kneeling at left-centre with the dagger lowered in his left hand, held away from his body, and his right arm hanging; the old priest's arm locked around the heir in the sanctum doorway beside the pillar; the dog flattened against the far wall; and clear wall and foliage across the top of the frame for two captions.

decisions.issues: Minor: a second, older arm in a white cloth with a red border enters at the left edge. It reads as the chaver's arm, which the script does not ask for. The assistant's arm on the right shows a sliver of white cloth at the shoulder. Otherwise the beat reads: an open hand and bare forearm on the stone, the fallen torch guttering in spilled oil (not blood), sanctum at left and tree at right, at night. There is no text, and the panel carries no lettering.

v01 (the only candidate) shows blood, which the script forbids for this panel ('No blood rendered'). Varma's brow cut is a red gash, and red runs from the corner of his lip. Nagoji also has red at his lip and a red wound on the back of his left hand. Varma has no sandal paste, and his hair is loose curls with no side knot above the LEFT ear. The chaver's body he is easing off is not in the frame. Nagoji's right arm is not clamped to his side and his left hand is not clenched over the cut palm. The framing and setting are good: Varma on the left on all fours, Nagoji on the right rising, sanctum at left, tree at right, a clear upper wall.
decisions.correction: Draw no blood anywhere: no red cut, drip, trickle or smear on either man. Show Varma's injury only through the line of white sandal paste across his brow, cracked and split apart by a cut drawn in ink only (no red), and a visibly swollen lower lip. Nagoji's lip and hands are unmarked. Varma's black hair is gathered in a side knot above his LEFT ear, not loose, and his right shoulder sits visibly lower than the left. Place the chaver's body at the lower left, face down on the flags, bare-chested with a white waist cloth and no blood, so that Varma is pushing himself up off it. Nagoji's right arm hangs straight, clamped against his side. His left hand is closed into a fist, with the fingers curled over the cut palm so the palm cannot be seen. Keep what worked: the two-shot with Varma on the left and Nagoji on the right getting to his feet; Nagoji's high topknot with grey temples, moustache, clean chin, silver chain and gold ear stud; Varma's moustache, pearl earring and one gold chain; the sanctum, jasmine and niche lamps behind; the jackfruit tree at right; and the plain upper wall clear for two short balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Varma's black hair is wavy and gathered in a knot at the back of his head rather than combed sleek into a knot above the LEFT ear. His moustache is fuller than the sheet's thin waxed one, and the white sandal paste on his brow is intact rather than split. The swollen lip shows as a dark bruise, not blood. Otherwise the beat is right: the elderly grey-bearded priest with trembling hands, Varma stopping him with an open palm (pearl earring, one gold chain, cream mundu, no crest or spear), the sanctum at left and the jackfruit tree at right. The hands are sound, and the night sky and upper wall are clear for the balloons.

Acceptable, with minor misses only. Varma's sandal paste is intact, and the brow cut set up in 9.3 is not visible. His split lip reads only as a slightly full, darker lower lip, which matches the accepted 9.4. The rest is right and fixes the r1 failures. Varma sits on the left against the jackfruit trunk: moustache, pearl earring, one gold chain, side knot, cream mundu, no crest or spear. His fingertips test his lip and his eyes go to the pillar, where the heir peers out (small white mundu, topknot, thin gold chain). Nagoji sits on the right with his back to the trunk: high topknot with grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold stud and silver chain. His RIGHT arm hangs limp to the flags. His LEFT palm lies open with a thin dark cut and no red, and the brand and white scar show on that inner left forearm only. The chaver lies face down at lower left with empty hands, and the dagger lies before Nagoji's feet. There is no blood or text. Night sky and dark palms above Varma's head leave room for the long balloon, and the wall below it has room for the short one.

v03 is the only candidate and it is acceptable. Nagoji matches his sheet: high topknot with grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold stud, and the silver chain with its medallion. His right shoulder is bound in cream cloth and his right hand rests limp on his knee. His left palm is held out palm up and the old priest is wrapping it. Varma matches his sheet: thick moustache, side knot above his left ear, pearl drop earrings, gold bead chain, bare chest, cream mundu with a gold border, no crest or spear. His head is tipped back with a wet cloth pressed to his brow. The priest is the same elderly priest with three ash stripes accepted in earlier rounds, with the brass pot and folded cloth beside him. The chaver's body lies face down in the lower-left foreground with the dagger beside it. There is no blood and no painted text. Nagoji's eyes are lowered toward the body. Minor deviations: (1) Varma sits on the shrine steps at screen left rather than leaning against the jackfruit bark. Nagoji is in the centre with the priest on the far right. This arrangement (shrine steps on the left, tree on the right) still matches 10.3 and 10.5. (2) The brand on the inner left forearm is a raised patch that is more pink-red than the pale patch on the sheet. It has the long white scar line and no emblem, and it reads as an old keloid scar rather than a wound. The open sky and wall across the top centre (about x 0.33 to 0.8, y 0 to 0.25) have room for both balloons. The doorway area above Varma can also take a balloon.

Acceptable, with minor issues. The brow mark is a vertical namam rather than a horizontal line of sandal paste split by a cut. The swollen lower lip is glossy red with a faint reddish smear below it, which reads as bruising and a split lip but is close to the no-blood limit. The hair knot sits behind the left ear rather than above it. Upper right (sky, leaves, lime-washed wall) and the mandapa roof at upper left give room for the two balloons away from the face.

Acceptable. The staging is right: Varma on the left, Nagoji on the right, and Nagoji's RIGHT shoulder bound. Nagoji's identity is correct: high topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, tiny gold stud, silver chain. Minor issues: Varma wears a cream upper cloth over his left shoulder across part of the chest, while 10.2 shows him fully bare-chested. His hair is gathered at the back and crown rather than in a side knot above the left ear, and he shows no split sandal paste or swollen lip. Nagoji's crossed wrists rest under one thick wrap, which reads mostly as a bandaged hand but could faintly suggest bound wrists. The wall and dark sky between and above the heads leave clear room for both balloons.

Acceptable, with minor issues. The framing is right: a close shot on Varma, eyes lowered to Nagoji's freshly wrapped hand in the near foreground. The brand is drawn correctly as a pale puckered patch beside the long white scar on the inner forearm, with no letters. Varma has his moustache, pearl drop earring, one gold chain and bare chest, plus the upper cloth seen in 10.3. Minor: his hair is loose curls bunched on the crown, not a side knot above the left ear, as in the accepted 10.2 and 10.3. The brow paste is a white line with a red mark rather than clearly split. The swollen lower lip has a small reddish bruise, close to but within the no-blood limit. By thumb position (palm toward the viewer, fingers pointing left, thumb on top), the wrapped hand is anatomically a RIGHT hand. With no body attached in this close shot, readers are unlikely to notice. The sky, foliage and lime-washed wall at the upper right give clear room for the balloon.

Acceptable. The cast is correct, with no doubles. Ramayyan (thin, receding hair, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle, tight face) comes down the top of the stair with two turbaned Nair torchbearers. The old priest, behind the pillar at right, has his arm around the heir (about ten, topknot, thin gold chain, white mundu). The chaver lies face down with his dagger, the only blade, and the young assistant lies fallen. There is no blood. Varma sits at left, smiling faintly, with pearl earrings and one gold chain. Nagoji sits beside him with the correct injuries: right arm in a sling at the shoulder and left palm wrapped. He has his high topknot, grey temples, thick moustache, clean chin, gold stud and silver chain. Minor: Varma's hair is loose curls, not a side knot. Nagoji's forearm scar is drawn pinkish rather than white. The priest has a full grey moustache and no short beard (10.1 is being regenerated). Ramayyan's balloon can sit in the dark sky and wall above him at top centre, and Varma's on the mandapa roof at the upper left or the peeling wall between Nagoji and the stair. Neither would cover a face.

Minor issues only. Varma's hair is drawn loose and swept back, and the side knot above his LEFT ear does not show; with his head tipped back for the physician it can pass as hidden. A wooden settee-like piece of furniture with turned posts sits in the background behind Varma, where the setting asks for no chairs or benches. It is period-plausible, not anachronistic. Otherwise sound. Varma has a stitched right brow, the cream cloth over his RIGHT shoulder, one gold chain, pearl drops and no crest. Nagoji has a topknot, thick moustache, clean chin, small gold stud, silver chain, his right arm bound across his chest, his left hand wrapped and the scar on his left forearm. Ramayyan stands between them with the bundle and stylus. The physician is elderly, in plain white, and is not the priest. Picketed horses show through the doorway. There is no text or gore. The large plain upper wall gives room for the caption and both of Ramayyan's balloons.

Minor: Varma's upper cloth hangs from his left shoulder instead of the injured right one, and he rests his chin on his right hand. The stitched cut runs up into his hairline. Otherwise the beat lands: Ramayyan slaps his palm on the bundle beside the jumping lamp flame and faces Varma, who sits bare-headed with his hair knotted, a pearl drop earring and a gold chain. The room, doorway and horses match the rest of the page, the hands are sound, and there is clear wall at the top for two short balloons.

These are small issues and none of them fails the panel. Nagoji's hair is a loose curly mass with only a small knot at the crown, not a neat high topknot, and his temples show no grey. The bandage covers his left wrist more than his palm. Ramayyan's stylus points across the space in front of Varma. His gaze and Nagoji's answering look still make it read as aimed at Nagoji. Everything else is right. Nagoji has the curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, the gold stud and the silver chain, his right arm is in a sling, and the scar shows on his inner left forearm. Varma is bare-headed with the side knot above his left ear, a stitched brow with no blood, pearl drops and one gold chain, and the cream cloth over his right shoulder. Ramayyan is thin and receding, in plain white, with the stylus and palm-leaf bundle. The doorway shows the torchlit courtyard with the picketed horses. There is plenty of plain wall in the upper left and upper centre for both balloons.

Minor: the upper cloth hangs from Varma's left shoulder, not the injured right one. He stands just inside, beside the open doorway, rather than in it. The table behind him is taller than the low table in panels 11.2 to 11.4. His black hair has a slight grey sheen, though it reads as black. Otherwise correct: risen, back half to us, turning his head over his shoulder, bare-headed with his hair knotted, a stitched cut on his right brow, the namam, a pearl drop earring and a gold chain, the torchlit courtyard with horses picketed in a long line beyond, and a large clear wall area at left for two balloons.

Minor issues only. v02 fixes all three round-1 failures. Nagoji is now bare-chested in a cream mundu and shoulder cloth, with no ochre tunic. His right arm is bound (upper-arm bandage) and his left hand and wrist are wrapped. The camera now looks in from the dark courtyard, so no courtyard, horses or torches show. Remaining small faults: (1) Varma's cream cloth again hangs from his LEFT shoulder (viewer-left in this back view), not the injured right one. This matches the accepted 11.5 back view but not 12.3. (2) His hair is a loose curly mass with the knot at the upper left of the crown. That is curlier than his sheet, though the face is hidden, so he cannot be mistaken for Nagoji. (3) He is warmly lit, not a true silhouette. (4) Nagoji's right arm hangs bandaged instead of being slung across his chest. Good: Nagoji has a high topknot with grey temples, thick curled moustache, a near-clean chin with light stubble, a tiny gold stud, silver chain, and is looking up. Ramayyan matches his sheet, by the low table with bundle and stylus. Varma has a pearl drop earring and a gold bead chain. Brass open-wick lamp and woven mats. No text. A large plain lime-washed wall above Nagoji and Ramayyan holds both Varma balloons, with tails toward the back-view head at upper left.

Minor: Varma's mostly black hair has visible grey streaks at the crown and temple, against the MUST MATCH 'black hair, never grey'. His forehead mark is the sheet's vertical namam, not a horizontal line of sandal paste. Everything else is right: shot through a large soft lamp flame, a serious face, a stitched brow without blood, one gold chain, pearl drop earrings, the cloth over his right shoulder, a knot behind the left ear, the same room and doorway with picketed horses, and no text. Minor issues only. v02 fixes the round-1 failures. Varma no longer looks like Nagoji's twin: his black hair is wavy, not curly, with no crown bun, and his cream cloth lies over his RIGHT shoulder. Nagoji's RIGHT arm (nearer Varma) is folded across his chest in a cream sling knotted over his left shoulder, and his left upper arm is bare. He looks down at his linen-wrapped LEFT palm. Small faults: (1) Varma's hair hangs loose to the nape, and no side knot is visible (it would sit above the hidden left ear). (2) His split lip does not read, so the smile looks easy rather than pained. (3) The brow stitches are a short cut with tiny cross stitches. They read as stitches, not symbols. Good: Varma has a pearl drop earring, one gold bead chain, a gold-bordered cream cloth and is bare-chested. Nagoji has a high topknot with grey temple, thick curled moustache, a near-clean chin, a tiny gold stud and silver chain. The brass open-wick lamp sits on the low table with an unmarked palm-leaf bundle and cups. The open doorway shows the torchlit picketed horses. No text, sound hands. Framing differs from the script. Ramayyan is a sharp, full mid-ground figure with his hand raised, not a blurred hand in the foreground, and the head shake reads as a sideways turn. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch22 row: high topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold stud, silver chain, right arm bound across his lap and left wrist wrapped. He looks off to the right toward the king off panel. Ramayyan matches his sheet and keeps the bundle and stylus. v01 (only candidate) breaks Nagoji's ch22 bible row (right shoulder bound, left palm wrapped). His torso faces the viewer, so the arm on the image-left side of his body is his RIGHT arm, and it is stretched out freely in a broad open-palm gesture toward Varma with only a wrist bandage. The binding sits on his LEFT upper arm instead (the brand scar is on that forearm, which confirms the side). His useless right arm gesturing is a visible continuity error. Secondary problems: Varma's cream cloth is over his LEFT shoulder instead of the injured right one, and his stitched brow is barely visible. Nagoji's chain is a heavy plain link chain that reads close to a shackle chain. What works: the composition, Ramayyan (very still at the left edge with bundle and stylus), the torchlit picketed horses through the doorway, the lamp and table, Nagoji's face (moustache, near-clean chin, gold stud, topknot) and Varma's pearl earrings and gold chain.
decisions.correction: Nagoji's RIGHT arm must be visibly immobilised and still: his right arm, the one on the side of his body nearer Varma and the lamp, is folded flat across his chest in a cream cloth sling knotted over his right shoulder, with the hand tucked into the sling. It makes no gesture and is not stretched out. Only his LEFT hand may move. If he gestures toward Varma, he does it with his LEFT hand, which crosses in front of his body, and its palm is wrapped in clean linen. There is no binding on his left upper arm. His silver chain of office is a fine silver chain, not a heavy iron-looking link chain. Drape Varma's cream cloth over his RIGHT shoulder (the shoulder away from Nagoji) and show a small stitched cut on his brow. Keep everything else that worked: Varma seated cross-legged on the left with pearl drop earrings, one thin gold chain and a cream gold-bordered mundu. Keep Ramayyan seated very still at the far left edge with his palm-leaf bundle and stylus, the low table with the brass open-wick lamp, cups and palm-leaf bundle, the open doorway onto the torchlit courtyard with picketed horses, the night lamplight, and the plain upper wall for lettering.

decisions.issues: Minor issues only. The beat is correct: his right upper arm is bandaged and the forearm lies across his body, and his wrapped left hand grips the silver chain. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, near-clean chin with light stubble, tiny gold stud, high topknot, grey at the temple. Three small issues: (1) the chain is drawn as an ornate rosette-link chain with a lion medallion, while the other panels in this room show a plainer chain; (2) Ramayyan is sharp rather than out of focus; (3) the right forearm crosses his waist rather than his chest. Clean. This is a tight insert of Ramayyan's hands, with the stylus cutting faint lamplit grooves into a palm leaf on the low table. The marks are abstract lines with no pseudo-text. v01 (only candidate) misses the script's explicit beat that both men toast left-handed. Varma's torso faces the viewer, and the arm holding his cup comes from his image-left shoulder, the one under the cream shoulder cloth. That is his injured RIGHT arm, swung across his chest in a full toast. Nagoji correctly toasts with his wrapped LEFT hand across his body. But his RIGHT arm is unbound and hanging bare, while a bandage wraps his LEFT upper arm, which breaks the bible row (right shoulder bound). The brand on his left forearm is drawn as a dark round tattoo-like stamp, not a pale puckered patch. What works: the cups meeting over the lamp, Varma's one-eye wince mid-laugh with a stitched brow, his pearl drop earrings and gold bead chain, Nagoji's face, stud, topknot and silver chain, the torchlit horses through the doorway, and clear upper wall and sky for lettering.
decisions.correction: Both men toast LEFT-handed. Varma sits on the left facing right. He raises his cup in his LEFT hand, the arm on the side of his body nearer Nagoji. His RIGHT arm, under the cream cloth draped over his injured right shoulder, stays lowered and still in his lap and does not hold a cup. Nagoji sits on the right facing left. He raises his cup in his LEFT hand, its palm wrapped in clean linen, crossing in front of his body. His RIGHT arm, the one on the side of his body nearer Varma, is folded across his chest in a cream cloth sling knotted over his right shoulder. There is no bandage on his left upper arm. Draw the brand on Nagoji's inner left forearm as a pale puckered patch of raised ridges, not a dark round stamp or tattoo. Keep everything else that worked: the two brass cups meeting large above the open-wick lamp at the centre of the frame, Varma wincing mid-laugh with one eye squeezed shut, the small stitched cut on his brow, his pearl drop earrings, one gold bead chain and bare head with his hair knotted up. Keep Nagoji's high topknot, tiny gold ear stud, silver chain, thick curled moustache and clean chin, the open doorway onto the torchlit courtyard with picketed horses, and the plain upper wall and dark sky for lettering.

decisions.issues: Minor: Nagoji has no visible silver chain of office, and no grey at the temples, though both show in 14.2. Everything else is right. Minor: a white cloth wrap on Nagoji's right wrist, although the script says no bandage. It reads as a rider's wrist wrap, not an injury. The chain of office is drawn dark steel-grey rather than bright silver. Otherwise right: the column of white-turbaned, white-clad lancers rides on a palm-lined coastal track under a heavy monsoon sky. The red standard with the silver conch carries no writing. Minor only. The water runs to the horses' bellies rather than their knees. The ear ornament is a small round gold bead on the lobe, which reads as a stud.
